# Upgrading OfficeIMO

<!-- officeimo-api-map:begin -->
## OfficeIMO and PSWriteOffice 3.6

OfficeIMO 3.6 and PSWriteOffice 3.6 change the public API in both languages and are released together. Nothing keeps a compatibility wrapper, so update scripts and code with the rules and tables below. PSWriteOffice goes from 594 commands and 383 aliases to 482 commands and 176 aliases; every job that worked before still works, usually through fewer commands. The [API design](Docs/officeimo.api-design.md) explains the rules.

### What changed

For PowerShell scripts:

- **Lifecycle.** Every authoring format has `New-Office{Format}`, `Open-Office{Format}`, `Save-Office{Format}` and `Close-Office{Format}`. With a content block, `New-` and `Open-` save and close the file when the block ends; if the block throws, nothing is saved. Without a block they return the live document. `-NoSave` is removed, `Get-Office{Format}` commands that opened files become `Open-`, and `-Open` becomes `-Show`. `New-` refuses to replace an existing file unless you add `-Force`.
- **Paths.** `-Path` is the input file when a command reads one (with wildcards), otherwise the file it creates. `-LiteralPath` takes input without wildcard expansion and binds from `Get-ChildItem`. `-OutputPath` is always one output file and never silently becomes a folder; commands that write several files take `-OutputDirectory`. `Export-` and `Convert-` replace an existing output unless you add `-NoClobber`.
- **One name per idea.** `-Document` replaces `-Presentation`, `-Workbook` and similar. `-Sheet` takes a name, a 1-based position or a sheet and replaces `-SheetName`/`-SheetIndex`; select a sheet named `1` with `-Sheet '1'`. Charts read `-Category` and `-Value` instead of `-CategoryProperty` and `-SeriesProperty`.
- **Switches instead of `$true`.** On/off parameters are switches: write `-KeepWithNext`, not `-KeepWithNext $true`. `-Bold:$false` still turns formatting off explicitly, and defaults that are on are turned off with `-No{Feature}` switches such as `-NoFreeze` and `-NoAutoFit`.
- **Lengths.** A bare number means points; a unit is written directly: `-Width 5cm`, `-SpacingBefore 12pt`, `-Margin 1in`. Parameter names no longer carry units, so `-WidthCm`, `-HeightPixels` and `-SpacingBeforePoints` become `-Width`, `-Height` and `-SpacingBefore`. Excel column widths stay in characters.
- **Positions are 1-based** everywhere: pages, slides, sheets, sections, table rows and columns, list items and insert positions. Scripts that passed 0-based indexes must add one.
- **Passwords.** `-Password` is a `SecureString`. It also accepts a plain string, with a warning, or a `PSCredential`, whose password is used. There is no separate `-Credential` parameter.
- **Themes by default.** New documents start from the `Modern` theme; choose another with `-Theme` (a built-in name, a theme object or a template path). Opening an existing document never restyles it.
- **Loss handling.** Converting to another format reports what could not be carried and continues; add `-FailOnLoss` to make loss an error. Saving a document in its own format fails if content would be lost; add `-AllowLoss` to accept it.
- **Options.** Option objects come from `New-Office{Format}{Purpose}Options`, and every `-Options` parameter also accepts a hashtable of option property names. Unknown keys are errors.
- **Content blocks.** Styled text is written with child commands (`WordText`, `PowerPointText`, `PdfText`, `ExcelText`); `-Run` hashtables of parallel arrays are removed. Each DSL command has exactly one alias, with the format name spelled out: `PowerPointSlide` replaces `PptSlide`. Plural, spelling, verb-last and unprefixed alias twins are removed.
- **`-WhatIf` and `-Confirm`** cover file-system effects: `New`, `Save`, `Export`, `Convert`, `Repair`, `Protect` and `Remove` commands.
- **Electronic invoices** are no longer part of PSWriteOffice (13 commands and aliases removed). Use the OfficeIMO.Invoicing packages from .NET.
- **Removed-command hints.** When a script calls a command or alias that no longer exists, PSWriteOffice prints its replacement, taken from the reference tables below.

For .NET code:

- **Lifecycle.** Every document type, including `PdfDocument`, is created with `Create`, opened with `Load` or `LoadAsync`, saved with `Save` or `SaveAsync`, and disposed with `using`. Options are `{Format}CreateOptions`, `{Format}LoadOptions` and `{Format}SaveOptions`.
- **One authoring model.** `AsFluent()`, `WordFluentDocument`, `ExcelFluentWorkbook` and their builders are removed; use the object model. `Add*` methods return what they create, and `AddImage` is the only image verb. Excel's `SheetComposer` stays, reached through `sheet.Report()`.
- **Conversions** are called on the source: `SaveAs{Target}(path or stream)` writes the file and returns `OfficeConversionReport`; `To{Target}()` returns the target model. The throwing and `...Result` pairs merge. `OfficeConverter` is the entry point for file-to-file and batch work.
- **Units and colors.** Geometry takes `OfficeLength` (`OfficeLength.Centimeters(2.5)`, `OfficeLength.Parse("12pt")`) instead of raw EMUs, twips or unit-suffixed parameters. `OfficeColor` is the only color type and moves to the `OfficeIMO` namespace.
- **Packages.** Format packages no longer carry other format engines, and `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` and `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf` change direction. See [.NET packages](#net-packages).

### Common jobs

Each job lists the commands a typical script uses, what they become and the parameters that change, followed by the new form.

#### Export objects to Excel

`Export-OfficeExcel` keeps its name and becomes styled by default: a themed table with a frozen header and fitted columns. `-NoFreeze`, `-NoAutoFit` and `-NoTableStyle` turn each default off. Typed column switches merge into `-ColumnFormat`, flattening settings into `-FlattenOptions`, document properties into `-DocumentProperty` and save switches into `-SaveOptions`.

| 3.5 | 3.6 | Parameter changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Export-OfficeExcel` | `Export-OfficeExcel` | `-WorksheetName` &rarr; `-Sheet`<br>`-StartRow`, `-StartColumn` &rarr; `-Address`<br>`-AutoFit` &rarr; `-NoAutoFit`<br>`-FreezeTopRow` &rarr; `-NoFreeze`<br>`-AppendToTable` &rarr; `-TableName`<br>`-ClearSheet` &rarr; `-ReplaceSheet`<br>`-TextColumn`, `-NumberColumn`, `-IntegerColumn`, `-PercentColumn`, `-CurrencyColumn`, `-DateColumn`, `-DateTimeColumn`, `-IncludeHeaderInColumnFormat` &rarr; `-ColumnFormat`<br>`-FormatDecimals` &rarr; `-Decimals`<br>`-FormatCultureName` &rarr; `-Culture`<br>`-DictionaryEntrySeparator`, `-DictionaryKeyValueSeparator`, `-MaxCollectionItems`, `-MaxNestingDepth`, `-IncludeUnexportableProperties`, `-PropertyConversionErrorAction` &rarr; `-FlattenOptions`<br>`-Open` &rarr; `-Show`<br>`-DocumentTitle`, `-Author`, `-Subject`, `-Keywords`, `-Description`, `-Category`, `-Company`, `-Manager`, `-ApplicationName`, `-LastModifiedBy` &rarr; `-DocumentProperty`<br>`-SafePreflight`, `-SafeRepairDefinedNames`, `-ValidateOpenXml`, `-DisableFastPackageWriter`, `-EvaluateFormulas`, `-ClearCachedFormulaResults`, `-MarkFormulasDirty`, `-ForceFullCalculationOnOpen` &rarr; `-SaveOptions`<br>`-TableName` (same name, changed)<br>Removed: `-AutoFitFormattedColumn`, `-BoldTopRow` |

```powershell
Get-Process | Export-OfficeExcel -Path .\Processes.xlsx -Show

# Export a titled sales sheet
$export = @{
    Path         = '.\Reports\Q3-Sales.xlsx'
    Sheet        = 'Orders'
    Table        = 'Orders'
    Title        = 'Q3 orders'
    ColumnFormat = @{ Margin = 'Percent' }
}
Import-OfficeCsv -Path .\Data\Q3-Orders.csv |
    Select-Object OrderId, Customer, Region, OrderDate, Amount, Margin |
    Export-OfficeExcel @export
```

#### Read rows from a workbook

`Import-OfficeExcel` is the one command that reads rows. `-Sheet` takes a name or a 1-based position, and `-Range` and `-Table` narrow the read.

| 3.5 | 3.6 | Parameter changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Get-OfficeExcelData` | `Import-OfficeExcel` | `-AsHashtable` &rarr; `-As` |
| `Get-OfficeExcelRange` | `Import-OfficeExcel` | `-HeadersInFirstRow` &rarr; `-NoHeader`<br>`-AsHashtable`, `-AsDataTable` &rarr; `-As`<br>`-SheetIndex` &rarr; `-Sheet` |
| `Import-OfficeExcel` | `Import-OfficeExcel` | `-WorksheetName`, `-SheetIndex`, `-AllSheets` &rarr; `-Sheet`<br>`-StartRow`, `-EndRow`, `-StartColumn`, `-EndColumn` &rarr; `-Range`<br>`-AsHashtable`, `-AsDataTable`, `-AsDataReader`, `-ByColumn` &rarr; `-As`<br>`-CultureName` &rarr; `-Culture` |

```powershell
Import-OfficeExcel -Path .\Book.xlsx -Range A1:D20
Import-OfficeExcel -Path .\Book.xlsx -Range B2:F40 -As DataTable
Import-OfficeExcel -Path .\Book.xlsx -Sheet Data -Range A1:D20

# Find the largest open orders
Import-OfficeExcel -Path .\Reports\Q3-Sales.xlsx -Sheet Orders -Range A5 |
    Where-Object Status -eq 'Open' |
    Sort-Object Amount -Descending |
    Select-Object -First 10 OrderId, Customer, Region, Amount
```

#### Open, save and close documents

Commands that opened a file with `Get-` are now `Open-`. With a content block, `New-` and `Open-` save and close the file when the block ends. Without a block they return the live document, which you save with `Save-` and close with `Close-`. `-NoSave` is gone, and `-Open` becomes `-Show`.

| 3.5 | 3.6 | Parameter changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Get-OfficeWord` | `Open-OfficeWord` |   |
| `Get-OfficeExcel` | `Open-OfficeExcel` | `-Password` (same name, changed) |
| `Get-OfficePowerPoint` | `Open-OfficePowerPoint` | `-Password` (same name, changed) |
| `Save-OfficeExcel` | `Save-OfficeExcel` | `-SafePreflight`, `-SafeRepairDefinedNames`, `-ValidateOpenXml`, `-DisableFastPackageWriter`, `-EvaluateFormulas`, `-ClearCachedFormulaResults`, `-MarkFormulasDirty`, `-ForceFullCalculationOnOpen` &rarr; `-SaveOptions`<br>`-Open` &rarr; `-Show`<br>Removed: `-DateSystem` |

```powershell
$doc = Open-OfficeWord -Path .\Report.docx
Open-OfficeExcel -Path .\Book.xlsx
$ppt = Open-OfficePowerPoint -Path .\Deck.pptx
$workbook | Save-OfficeExcel -Path .\Copy.xlsx

# Rebrand every contract in a folder
Get-ChildItem -Path .\Contracts -Filter *.docx | Open-OfficeWord -PassThru {
    Update-OfficeWordText -OldValue 'Contoso Ltd' -NewValue 'Contoso Group plc'
    Set-OfficeWordDocumentProperty -Name LegalEntity -Value 'Contoso Group plc' -Custom
}

# Add the latest tickets to a tracker
$newTickets = Import-OfficeCsv -Path .\Exports\Tickets-2026-10-26.csv
Open-OfficeExcel -Path .\Reports\Helpdesk.xlsx {
    ExcelSheet 'Tickets' {
        Add-OfficeExcelTableRow -Table Tickets -InputObject $newTickets
        ExcelConditionalFormat -Header AgeDays -Table Tickets -Color Accent2
    }
}
```

#### Write Word documents

Styled runs are child commands. Replace `-Run @{ Text = ...; Bold = ... }` hashtables of parallel arrays with `WordText` commands inside `WordParagraph`. The same pattern applies to `PowerPointText`, `PdfText` and `ExcelText`.

| 3.5 | 3.6 | Parameter changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `New-OfficeWord` | `New-OfficeWord` | `-Open` &rarr; `-Show`<br>`-TemplatePath` &rarr; `-Template`<br>Removed: `-NoSave` |
| `Add-OfficeWordParagraph` | `Add-OfficeWordParagraph` | `-Target` &rarr; `-Document`<br>Removed: `-Run` |
| `Add-OfficeWordText` | `Add-OfficeWordText` | `-Strike` &rarr; `-Strikethrough`<br>`-FontSize` &rarr; `-Size`<br>`-FontName`, `-FontFamily`, `-Typeface` &rarr; `-Font`<br>Removed: `-Run` |

```powershell
$doc = New-OfficeWord -Path .\Report.docx   # no block = live document
WordParagraph { WordText 'Status: ' -Bold; WordText 'Ready' -Color Success }
WordParagraph { WordText 'Important: ' -Bold; WordText 'read first' -Italic }

# Build a themed status report
$milestones = Import-Csv -Path .\Data\Northwind-Milestones.csv
$trend = Import-Csv -Path .\Data\Northwind-Trend.csv

New-OfficeWord -Path .\Reports\Northwind-Status.docx -Theme Modern -Show {
    WordHeading 'Northwind migration'
    WordParagraph {
        WordText 'Overall status: ' -Bold
        WordText 'On track' -Bold -Color Success
    }
    WordTable -InputObject $milestones {
        WordTableCondition { $_.Status -eq 'At risk' } -BackgroundColor Danger
    }
    WordChart -Type Line -InputObject $trend -Category Week -Value Complete -Title 'Completion by week'
    WordFooter {
        WordText 'Internal · Page '
        WordPageNumber -IncludeTotal
    }
}

# Mix styled runs and paragraph spacing
New-OfficeWord -Path .\Reports\Maintenance-Notice.docx {
    WordParagraph {
        Set-OfficeWordParagraph -SpacingAfter 12pt -KeepWithNext
        WordText 'Planned maintenance: '
        WordText 'Saturday 2 November, 22:00-02:00 UTC' -Bold
        WordText '. Email and the intranet will be unavailable.'
    }
    WordParagraph 'Questions go to the service desk.' -Alignment Center
}
```

#### Build PowerPoint decks without coordinates

Slides are built from theme layouts. `-Layout` is optional: the layout is chosen from the slide content, and the first slide uses the title layout. Deck plans and the designer deck fold into `New-OfficePowerPoint` and `PowerPointSlide`. `-X`, `-Y`, `-Width` and `-Height` remain for deliberate placement and take lengths such as `2cm`.

| 3.5 | 3.6 | Parameter changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `New-OfficePowerPoint` | `New-OfficePowerPoint` | `-Open` &rarr; `-Show`<br>`-Password` (same name, changed)<br>Removed: `-NoSave` |
| `Add-OfficePowerPointSlide` | `Add-OfficePowerPointSlide` | `-Presentation` &rarr; `-Document`<br>`-Layout`, `-LayoutName`, `-LayoutType` &rarr; `-TemplateLayout`<br>Removed: `-CaseSensitive` |
| `Add-OfficePowerPointBullets` | `Add-OfficePowerPointList` | `-Bullets` &rarr; `-Items`<br>`-Level`, `-Slide` (same name, changed) |
| `Add-OfficePowerPointTextBox` | `Add-OfficePowerPointTextBox` | `-Run` &rarr; `-Content` |
| `New-OfficePowerPointDeckPlan` | `New-OfficePowerPoint` | `-Content` (same name, changed) |
| `Add-OfficePowerPointDesignerDeck` | `Add-OfficePowerPointSlide` | `-Presentation` &rarr; `-Document`<br>`-AccentColor` &rarr; `New-OfficePowerPoint -Accent`<br>`-Seed` &rarr; `New-OfficePowerPoint -Seed`<br>`-Purpose` &rarr; `New-OfficePowerPoint -Purpose`<br>`-Eyebrow` &rarr; `Add-OfficePowerPointSlide -Eyebrow`<br>`-FooterLeft` &rarr; `Add-OfficePowerPointFooter -Alignment Left`<br>`-FooterRight` &rarr; `Add-OfficePowerPointFooter -Alignment Right`<br>`-CreativeDirectionPack` &rarr; `New-OfficePowerPoint -Style`<br>`-LayoutStrategy` &rarr; `New-OfficePowerPoint -LayoutStrategy`<br>Removed: `-Plan`, `-Name`, `-AlternativeCount`, `-NoApplyTheme`, `-Preview` |

```powershell
New-OfficePowerPoint -Path .\Review.pptx -Theme Boardroom { PowerPointSlide -Title 'Quarterly review' }
PowerPointSlide -Title 'Agenda' { PowerPointList -Items 'Results','Risks' }
PowerPointList -Items 'Wins','Risks'   # or PowerPointList { PowerPointListItem 'Wins' }
PowerPointTextBox -X 2cm -Y 4cm -Width 10cm { PowerPointText 'Status: ' -Bold; PowerPointText 'On track' -Color Success }
New-OfficePowerPoint -Path .\Deck.pptx { PowerPointSlide -Title 'Service Review'; PowerPointSlide -Title 'Rhythm' { PowerPointStep 'Collect' 'Gather signals' } }
New-OfficePowerPoint -Path .\Deck.pptx -Accent '#0F766E' -Purpose 'monthly service brief' { PowerPointSlide -Title 'Service Review' }

# Build a quarterly review without coordinates
$sales = Import-OfficeExcel -Path .\Reports\Q3-Sales.xlsx -Sheet 'By region'
$priorities = Import-OfficeExcel -Path .\Reports\Q3-Sales.xlsx -Sheet 'Priorities'
New-OfficePowerPoint -Path .\Reports\Q3-Review.pptx -Theme Boardroom -Show {
    PowerPointFooter {
        PowerPointText 'Contoso | Internal | Slide '
        PowerPointSlideNumber
    }
    PowerPointSlide -Title 'Q3 business review' -Subtitle 'Performance, decisions and priorities'
    PowerPointSlide -Title 'Quarter at a glance' {
        PowerPointKpi '$4.2M' 'Revenue' -Change '+12% vs Q2' -Trend Up
        PowerPointKpi '38%' 'Gross margin' -Change '+2 pt' -Trend Up
        PowerPointKpi '1,284' 'New customers' -Change '+9%' -Trend Up
    }
    PowerPointSlide -Title 'Revenue and margin by region' {
        PowerPointChart -InputObject $sales -Category Region -Value Revenue -Type Column -Title 'Revenue (USD k)'
        PowerPointChart -InputObject $sales -Category Region -Value Margin -Type Line -Title 'Margin (%)'
        PowerPointNotes 'Start with EMEA: margin grew faster than revenue.'
    }
    PowerPointSlide -Title 'Next-quarter priorities' {
        PowerPointTable -InputObject $priorities -Property Priority, Owner, Due
    }
}

# Let the content choose each layout
$incidents = Import-OfficeExcel -Path .\Reports\Ops-October.xlsx -Sheet 'Incidents'
New-OfficePowerPoint -Path .\Reports\Service-Review-October.pptx -Theme Modern {
    PowerPointSlide -Title 'Service review' -Subtitle 'October 2026' -Eyebrow 'IT operations'
    PowerPointSlide -Title 'Health'
    PowerPointSlide -Title 'Service health' {
        PowerPointKpi '99.95%' 'Availability' -Change '+0.02 pt'
        PowerPointKpi '182 ms' 'Median latency' -Change '-14 ms'
        PowerPointKpi '7' 'Priority incidents' -Change '+2' -Color Warning
    }
    PowerPointSlide -Title 'Incidents by service' {
        PowerPointChart -InputObject $incidents -Category Service -Value Count -Type Bar
        PowerPointTable -InputObject $incidents -Property Service, Count, MeanTimeToRestore
    }
    PowerPointSlide -Title 'Change process' {
        PowerPointStep 'Request' 'Raised in the service desk'
        PowerPointStep 'Review' 'CAB approves risk and window'
        PowerPointStep 'Deploy' 'Automated with rollback'
        PowerPointStep 'Verify' 'Health checks close the change'
    }
}
```

#### Convert files

File-to-file `ConvertTo-*` and `ConvertFrom-*` commands and `Export-OfficeDocumentPdf` become `Convert-OfficeDocument -Path -To -OutputPath`. Format-specific settings go through `-Options`. Batches run in parallel with `-ThrottleLimit`, and `-Resume` continues an interrupted batch. `ConvertTo-OfficeMarkdown` and `ConvertTo-OfficeCsv` stay, because they turn objects into text rather than converting files.

| 3.5 | 3.6 | Parameter changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ConvertTo-OfficeDocument` | `Convert-OfficeDocument` | `-InputPath`, `-InputDirectory` &rarr; `-Path`<br>`-TargetExtension` &rarr; `-To`<br>`-SourceExtension` &rarr; `-Extension`<br>`-NoRecurse` &rarr; `-Recurse`<br>`-ConversionRouteId` &rarr; `-Route`<br>`-ConflictPolicy` &rarr; `-NoClobber`<br>`-ConversionOptions` &rarr; `-Options`<br>`-MaximumConcurrency` &rarr; `-ThrottleLimit`<br>`-CheckpointDirectory` &rarr; `-CheckpointPath`<br>`-OutputProfile`, `-MaximumFiles` (same name, changed)<br>Removed: `-ItemResults` |
| `Export-OfficeDocumentPdf` | `Convert-OfficeDocument` | `-InputPath`, `-InputPaths`, `-InputDirectory` &rarr; `-Path`<br>`-Path` &rarr; `-OutputPath`<br>`-SourceExtensions` &rarr; `-Extension`<br>`-NoRecurse` &rarr; `-Recurse`<br>`-WordOptions`, `-ExcelOptions`, `-PowerPointOptions`, `-MarkdownOptions`, `-RtfOptions`, `-HtmlOptions`, `-TextOptions` &rarr; `-Options`<br>`-Open` &rarr; `-Show`<br>`-ConversionRouteId` &rarr; `-Route`<br>`-ConflictPolicy` &rarr; `-NoClobber`<br>`-MaximumConcurrency` &rarr; `-ThrottleLimit`<br>`-CheckpointDirectory` &rarr; `-CheckpointPath`<br>Removed: `-SourceConversionReportVariable`, `-PdfWarningVariable`, `-PdfConversionReportVariable`, `-PassThru`, `-ItemResults` |
| `ConvertTo-OfficeWordMarkdown` | `Convert-OfficeDocument` | `-FontFamily` &rarr; `New-OfficeWordMarkdownOptions -Font`<br>`-EnableUnderline` &rarr; `New-OfficeWordMarkdownOptions -EnableUnderline`<br>`-EnableHighlight` &rarr; `New-OfficeWordMarkdownOptions -EnableHighlight`<br>`-ImageExportMode` &rarr; `New-OfficeWordMarkdownOptions -ImageExportMode`<br>`-ImageDirectory` &rarr; `New-OfficeWordMarkdownOptions -ImageDirectory` |
| `ConvertFrom-OfficeWordMarkdown` | `Convert-OfficeDocument` | `-TemplatePath` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -Template`<br>`-BookmarkName` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -BookmarkName`<br>`-ContentControlTag` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -ContentControlTag`<br>`-ContentControlAlias` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -ContentControlAlias`<br>`-KeepPlaceholder` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -KeepPlaceholder`<br>`-RenderFrontMatter` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -NoFrontMatter`<br>`-FontFamily` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -Font`<br>`-BaseUri` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -BaseUri`<br>`-AllowLocalImages` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -AllowLocalImages`<br>`-AllowedImageDirectory` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -AllowedImageDirectory`<br>`-AllowRemoteImages` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -AllowRemoteImages`<br>`-ReaderOptions` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -ReaderOptions`<br>`-Profile` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -Profile`<br>`-Theme` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -Theme`<br>`-AllowDataUriImages` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -NoDataUriImages`<br>`-MaxDataUriImageBytes` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -MaxDataUriImageBytes`<br>`-PreferNarrativeSingleLineDefinitions` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -PreferNarrativeSingleLineDefinitions`<br>`-FitImagesToPageContentWidth` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -FitImagesToPageContentWidth`<br>`-FitImagesToContextWidth` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -FitImagesToContextWidth`<br>`-MaxImageWidthPercentOfContent` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -MaxImageWidthPercentOfContent`<br>`-NormalizeInput` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -NoNormalizeInput`<br>`-MaxImageWidthPixels` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -MaxImageWidth`<br>`-MaxImageHeightPixels` &rarr; `New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -MaxImageHeight`<br>`-Markdown` &rarr; `-Text`<br>`-Open` &rarr; `-Show` |
| `ConvertTo-OfficePdfWord` | `Convert-OfficeDocument` | `-OutPath` &rarr; `-OutputPath`<br>`-Open` &rarr; `-Show`<br>`-FilePath` &rarr; `-Path`<br>`-IgnorePermissionRestrictions` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -IgnorePermissionRestrictions`<br>Removed: `-Force`, `-PassThruReport` |
| `ConvertTo-OfficeExcelHtml` | `Convert-OfficeDocument` | `-Workbook` &rarr; `-Document`<br>`-Profile`, `-Theme`, `-Title`, `-MaxRowsPerSheet`, `-EmptyCellText`, `-NoDefaultStyles` &rarr; `-Options`<br>`-Password`, `-OutputPath` (same name, changed) |

```powershell
Get-ChildItem .\Reports -Filter *.docx | Convert-OfficeDocument -To Pdf -OutputDirectory .\Pdf
Convert-OfficeDocument -Path .\Report.docx -OutputPath .\Report.pdf
Convert-OfficeDocument -Path .\report.docx -To Markdown -OutputPath .\report.md
Convert-OfficeDocument -Path .\SOP.md -To Word -OutputPath .\SOP.docx -Options (New-OfficeMarkdownWordOptions -Template .\Template.docx -BookmarkName MainContent)
Convert-OfficeDocument -Path .\In.pdf -To Word -OutputPath .\Out.docx -Options (New-OfficePdfWordOptions)
Convert-OfficeDocument -Path .\Book.xlsx -To Html -OutputPath .\Book.html -Options (New-OfficeExcelHtmlOptions -Profile SemanticTables)

# Convert one file to a named output
Convert-OfficeDocument .\Reports\Q3-Sales.docx .\Pdf\Q3-Sales.pdf
```

26 more commands and 14 aliases also map to `Convert-OfficeDocument`; the [reference tables](#powershell-reference) list each one.

#### Export pages, slides and sheets as images

The per-format `Export-Office*Image` commands become `Export-OfficeDocumentImage`. Several images go to `-OutputDirectory`; `-OutputPath` writes exactly one file and is never treated as a folder.

| 3.5 | 3.6 | Parameter changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Export-OfficeExcelChartImage` | `Export-OfficeDocumentImage` | `-WorksheetName` &rarr; `-Sheet`<br>`-ChartName` &rarr; `-Chart`<br>Removed: `-Force` |
| `Export-OfficeExcelImage` | `Export-OfficeDocumentImage` | `-OutputPath` &rarr; `-OutputDirectory`<br>`-Options` (same name, changed) |
| `Export-OfficeExcelRangeImage` | `Export-OfficeDocumentImage` | `-WorksheetName` &rarr; `-Sheet`<br>`-Range` (same name, changed)<br>Removed: `-Force` |
| `Export-OfficeHtmlImage` | `Export-OfficeDocumentImage` | `-Html` &rarr; `-Text`<br>`-DocumentOptions`, `-RenderOptions` &rarr; `-Options`<br>`-PageIndex` &rarr; `-Page`<br>`-Document` (same name, changed)<br>Removed: `-PassThru` |
| `Export-OfficePdfImage` | `Export-OfficeDocumentImage` | `-OutputPath` &rarr; `-OutputDirectory`<br>`-PageRange` &rarr; `-Page`<br>`-ReadOptions` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -LoadOptions`<br>`-IgnorePermissionRestrictions` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -IgnorePermissionRestrictions`<br>Removed: `-PassThru` |
| `Export-OfficePowerPointImage` | `Export-OfficeDocumentImage` | `-Presentation` &rarr; `-Document`<br>`-OutputPath` &rarr; `-OutputDirectory`<br>`-Format`, `-Options` (same name, changed)<br>Removed: `-PassThru` |
| `Export-OfficeVisioImage` | `Export-OfficeDocumentImage` | `-OutputPath` &rarr; `-OutputDirectory` |
| `Export-OfficeWordImage` | `Export-OfficeDocumentImage` | `-AllPages` &rarr; `-OutputDirectory` |

```powershell
Export-OfficeDocumentImage -Path .\Book.xlsx -Sheet Data -Chart Revenue -OutputPath .\chart.png
Export-OfficeDocumentImage -Path .\Book.xlsx -Sheet Data -OutputDirectory .\Png
Export-OfficeDocumentImage -Path .\Book.xlsx -Sheet Data -Range A1:F20 -OutputPath .\range.png
Export-OfficeDocumentImage -Path .\page.html -OutputDirectory .\img -Options (New-OfficeHtmlRenderOptions -ViewportWidth 1280px)
Export-OfficeDocumentImage -Path .\In.pdf -OutputDirectory .\Pages -Dpi 150
Export-OfficeDocumentImage -Path .\Deck.pptx -Page 1,3 -OutputDirectory .\Slides -Format Png
Export-OfficeDocumentImage -Path .\Map.vsdx -OutputDirectory .\Images -Format Png -Options (New-OfficeVisioImageOptions)
Export-OfficeDocumentImage -Path .\Report.docx -OutputDirectory .\Pages -Format Png -Page 1-2

# Render one chart to a single image
Export-OfficeDocumentImage -Path .\Reports\Q3-Sales.xlsx -Sheet Summary -Chart 'Revenue by region' -OutputPath .\Images\Revenue-by-Region.png -Dpi 200
```

#### Read and edit PDF files

`Get-OfficePdf` becomes `Open-OfficePdf` for editing. Reading text, structure and metadata uses the cross-format `Read-OfficeDocument` and `Get-OfficeDocumentInfo`, which work the same for every format.

| 3.5 | 3.6 | Parameter changes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Get-OfficePdf` | `Open-OfficePdf` | `-FilePath` &rarr; `-Path`<br>`-FullName` &rarr; `-LiteralPath`<br>`-LiteralPath` (same name, changed) |
| `Read-OfficePdf` | `Read-OfficeDocument` | `-FilePath` &rarr; `-Path`<br>`-Profile` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -Profile`<br>`-PageRange` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -Page`<br>`-Password` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -Password`<br>`-IgnorePermissionRestrictions` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -IgnorePermissionRestrictions`<br>`-Options` (same name, changed)<br>Removed: `-Document` |
| `Get-OfficePdfText` | `Read-OfficeDocument` | `-AsMarkdown` &rarr; `-As Markdown`<br>`-AsTextBlock` &rarr; `-As Structure`<br>`-PageRange` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -Page`<br>`-Password` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -Password`<br>`-IgnorePermissionRestrictions` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -IgnorePermissionRestrictions`<br>`-FilePath` &rarr; `-Path`<br>`-FullName` &rarr; `-LiteralPath`<br>`-ByPage`, `-LiteralPath` (same name, changed)<br>Removed: `-OutputPath` |
| `Get-OfficePdfInfo` | `Get-OfficeDocumentInfo` | `-FilePath` &rarr; `-Path`<br>`-FullName` &rarr; `-LiteralPath`<br>`-IgnorePermissionRestrictions` &rarr; `New-OfficePdfReadOptions -IgnorePermissionRestrictions`<br>`-LiteralPath` (same name, changed) |

```powershell
$pdf = Open-OfficePdf -Path .\In.pdf
Read-OfficeDocument -Path .\In.pdf -As Structure -Options (New-OfficePdfReadOptions -Profile Structured)
Read-OfficeDocument -Path .\In.pdf -As Markdown | Set-Content .\In.md
Get-OfficeDocumentInfo -Path .\In.pdf

# Finalize a board pack in one block
Open-OfficePdf -Path .\Reports\Q3-Board-Pack.pdf -OutputPath .\Reports\Q3-Board-Pack-Final.pdf {
    Remove-OfficePdfPage -Page 2
    PdfMetadata -Title 'Q3 board pack' -Author 'Finance' -Subject 'Quarterly results'
    Add-OfficePdfStamp -Text 'BOARD CONFIDENTIAL' -Size 36 -Rotation 30 -Opacity 0.15 -Behind
}

# Chunk a knowledge base for AI ingestion
Read-OfficeDocument -Path .\Knowledge -Recurse -Extension .docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx -MaximumFiles 0 -As Chunks -MaximumChunkCharacters 1200 -ThrottleLimit 8 |
    ForEach-Object { $_ | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 -Compress } |
    Set-Content -Path .\Index\chunks.jsonl
```

### .NET packages

#### OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf and OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf change direction

`OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` and `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf` keep their package IDs but change direction. In 3.5 they convert PDF into the Office format; in 3.6 they export the Office format to PDF. Updating the version without changing code therefore gives a project a different API under the same package ID.

| Package | 3.5 content | 3.6 content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` | Moves to `OfficeIMO.Pdf.Word`: All current content: PdfWordConverterExtensions, PdfToWordOptions, PdfWordImportMode, PdfWordConversionReport/Result (PDF -&gt; Word reconstruction) | From `OfficeIMO.Word`: Layout/ (123 files, namespace OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf: WordPdfConverterExtensions\*, WordToPdfOptions, PdfExportWarning, PdfFootnote, TableLayout\*, LegacyDocPdfConverter)<br>From `OfficeIMO.Word`: Imaging/ (WordDocument.Imaging\*.cs, WordPageImageExport, WordImageExportOptions, WordDocumentVisualSnapshot, WordImageExportBuilder) |
| `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf` | Moves to `OfficeIMO.Pdf.PowerPoint`: All current content (PDF -&gt; PowerPoint reconstruction) | From `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint`: Layout/ (22 files: PowerPointPdfConverterExtensions\*, PowerPointToPdfOptions, PowerPointPdfExportWarning) |

- If you reference `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` to read PDF files into `OfficeIMO.Word` documents, reference `OfficeIMO.Pdf.Word` instead. If you export `OfficeIMO.Word` documents to PDF, add `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf`; the export no longer comes with `OfficeIMO.Word`.
- If you reference `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf` to read PDF files into `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint` documents, reference `OfficeIMO.Pdf.PowerPoint` instead. If you export `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint` documents to PDF, add `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf`; the export no longer comes with `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint`.

#### The OfficeIMO package

The `OfficeIMO` package is the front door for applications that want the common formats and conversions in one reference: `dotnet add package OfficeIMO`. It targets `netstandard2.0`, `net8.0`, `net10.0`, plus `net472` on Windows, the same as the format packages.

It references `OfficeIMO.Core`, `OfficeIMO.Word`, `OfficeIMO.Excel`, `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint`, `OfficeIMO.Pdf`, `OfficeIMO.Markdown`, `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf`, `OfficeIMO.Excel.Pdf`, `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf`, `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Html`, `OfficeIMO.Pdf.Word`, `OfficeIMO.Pdf.Excel`, `OfficeIMO.Pdf.PowerPoint`, `OfficeIMO.Word.Markdown`, `OfficeIMO.Word.Html`, `OfficeIMO.Markdown.Html`, `OfficeIMO.Markdown.Pdf`, `OfficeIMO.Reader.All`.

`OfficeConverter`, the batch types and the shared foundations, including `OfficeColor`, live in the `OfficeIMO` namespace. Format types keep their per-format namespaces.

#### Package moves

Format packages depend only on `OfficeIMO.Core` and their own third-party libraries. Conversions live in `OfficeIMO.{Source}.{Target}` adapter packages, and reconstruction from PDF lives in `OfficeIMO.Pdf.{Target}`.

| From | To | What moves | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OfficeIMO.Word` | `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` | Layout/ (123 files, namespace OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf: WordPdfConverterExtensions\*, WordToPdfOptions, PdfExportWarning, PdfFootnote, TableLayout\*, LegacyDocPdfConverter) | Format packages never depend on another format engine; conversions live in OfficeIMO.{Source}.{Target} adapters. |
| `OfficeIMO.Word` | `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` | Imaging/ (WordDocument.Imaging\*.cs, WordPageImageExport, WordImageExportOptions, WordDocumentVisualSnapshot, WordImageExportBuilder) | Word image export renders by calling document.ToPdfDocumentResult(), re-reading the bytes with PdfReadDocument.Open and rasterising through the internal PdfImageExportEngine. It depends on the PDF writer, reader and renderer, not just a layout engine. |
| `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` | `OfficeIMO.Pdf.Word` | All current content: PdfWordConverterExtensions, PdfToWordOptions, PdfWordImportMode, PdfWordConversionReport/Result (PDF -&gt; Word reconstruction) | The current OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf package is the reverse direction (PDF to Word). Reconstruction belongs in OfficeIMO.Pdf.Word. |
| `OfficeIMO.Excel.Pdf` | `OfficeIMO.Pdf.Excel` | PdfExcelTableConverterExtensions, PdfTablesToExcelOptions, PdfExcelTable\* (PDF tables -&gt; Excel) | Reconstruction from PDF lives in OfficeIMO.Pdf.Excel. |
| `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint` | `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf` | Layout/ (22 files: PowerPointPdfConverterExtensions\*, PowerPointToPdfOptions, PowerPointPdfExportWarning) | Format packages never depend on another format engine; conversions live in OfficeIMO.{Source}.{Target} adapters. |
| `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf` | `OfficeIMO.Pdf.PowerPoint` | All current content (PDF -&gt; PowerPoint reconstruction) | Reconstruction from PDF lives in OfficeIMO.Pdf.PowerPoint. |
| `OfficeIMO.Pdf` | `OfficeIMO.Pdf.Word` (new) | Reconstruction to Word now in OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf (PdfWordConverterExtensions, PdfToWordOptions, PdfWord\*) | Reconstruction from PDF lives in the matching OfficeIMO.Pdf.{Target} adapter. |
| `OfficeIMO.Reader.All` | `OfficeIMO` | OfficeDocumentPdfConverter (Email/EPUB/Visio to PDF facades) | OfficeConverter is the single file-to-file and batch entry point; it absorbs OfficeWorkflow.Convert, the OfficeDocumentPdfConverter facades and the \*ToPdfBytes helpers. |
| `OfficeIMO.Workflows` | `OfficeIMO` | Conversion and batch core: OfficeWorkflow.Convert/ConvertDirectory/ConvertFiles, OfficeConversionBatchBuilder, Batches/ (OfficeConversionBatchExecutor\*, report, serializers), ConversionJobs/, OfficeWorkflowRunner.Conversions/ConversionBatch/ConversionSerialization | OfficeConverter is the single file-to-file and batch entry point; it absorbs OfficeWorkflow.Convert, the OfficeDocumentPdfConverter facades and the \*ToPdfBytes helpers. |
| `OfficeIMO.Html.Pdf` | `OfficeIMO.Pdf.Html` | whole package (PDF to HTML conversion) | Adapter packages are named {Source}.{Target}; this package converts PDF to HTML, while HTML to PDF lives in OfficeIMO.Html. Newcomers install the wrong package for HTML to PDF. |

#### Removed dependencies

These packages stop bringing another engine. Reference the adapter that you use directly.

| Package | No longer references | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OfficeIMO.Word` | `OfficeIMO.Pdf` | Format packages never depend on another format engine; conversions live in OfficeIMO.{Source}.{Target} adapters. |
| `OfficeIMO.Word.Markdown` | `OfficeIMO.Word.Html`, `OfficeIMO.Markdown.Html` | Adapters do not chain through a third format; Markdown to Word should not need HTML. |
| `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint` | `OfficeIMO.Pdf` | Format packages never depend on another format engine; conversions live in OfficeIMO.{Source}.{Target} adapters. |

#### Target frameworks

Libraries retain `netstandard2.0`, `net8.0` and `net10.0`, with `net472` included on Windows. PSWriteOffice retains `net8.0` for PowerShell 7.4 and later, and `net472` for Windows PowerShell 5.1.

| Authoring | `OfficeIMO.Word.WordDocument.AddTable(int rows, int columns, WordTableStyle tableStyle = TableGrid)` | Changed | `OfficeIMO.Word.WordDocument.AddTable(int rows, int columns, WordTableStyle tableStyle = OfficeIMOModern)` | New tables follow the shared Modern theme. Pass TableGrid explicitly to retain cell grid borders. Body, section, header, footer, nested and paragraph-adjacent creation use the same default. Assigning a plain numeric value in an unaligned Modern table cell applies the theme numeric alignment; explicit alignment and rich text retain their formatting. Plain header labels over numeric columns follow the same theme alignment unless the header already has explicit alignment, a paragraph style or rich content. New OfficeIMOModern tables mark the first row as a repeating header (w:tblHeader), including in Word PDF output. Set table.RepeatHeaderRowAtTheTopOfEachPage = false to turn repetition off. Headerless object tables keep every row as body data; loading an existing table does not add a repeating header. HTML conversion preserves source body/header rows; PDF import honours the explicit RepeatHeaderRows setting, including with Modern tables. |

PdfSaveOptions.Encryption encrypts an unencrypted output after fidelity validation, for bytes, file, stream and async saves. Omission preserves existing security; the live document security configuration stays unchanged. Use document.Security.Reencrypt with the current owner password to replace existing encryption. ## Chart and workbook defaults

New workbooks use the default `OfficeTheme` font and palette: Aptos and the
Modern accents. Chart typography, gridlines, line widths and bar spacing follow
the shared theme. Regenerate worksheet and chart preview baselines; the default
font can also change column widths in pixels. Loaded documents keep their styles.

Line series created from `OfficeChartData` without a marker-visibility argument
follow the theme: Modern shows markers only for fewer than three points, while
Classic uses circles. Explicit visibility and point styling take precedence;
data-only updates retain existing native marker formatting.

Clearing PowerPoint axis-label text styling restores the theme's font, size and
colour while retaining label rotation. It no longer leaves those text properties
unset.

## PowerPoint composition defaults

Automatic card composition fits up to eight cards per slide and honors
`MaxColumns`. Set `PowerPointDeckContinuationOptions.CardsPerSlide = 6` to keep
the previous continuation limit.

## HTML paragraph spacing

The HTML engine gives `p` elements browser-default margins of `1em` above and
below, with adjacent margin collapse. Explicit CSS overrides these defaults.
Use `p { margin-top: 0 }` to keep the previous top spacing.

## Word new-document defaults

New documents take their heading styles from the default `OfficeTheme`: Heading 1
to 6 use the theme type scale, text colour and bold weight, with space after each
heading, and `Title` and `Subtitle` styles are defined. Apply them through
`WordParagraphStyles.Title` and `WordParagraphStyles.Subtitle`. `AddTable` sizes default
columns to the section's text width instead of 2400 twips each. Loaded documents
keep their own styles. To keep the previous look in a new document, set the
heading style definitions and column widths explicitly.

New tables use `WordTableStyle.OfficeIMOModern`: a tinted header, horizontal
rules and alternating body rows. Pass `WordTableStyle.TableGrid` explicitly to
keep the grid style. This applies to body, section, header, footer, nested and
paragraph-adjacent table creation. Assigning a plain numeric value in an
unaligned Modern table cell now applies the theme's numeric alignment. Set
`ParagraphAlignment` explicitly to choose a different alignment.

New `OfficeIMOModern` tables mark the first row as a repeating header (`w:tblHeader`),
including in Word PDF output. Set `table.RepeatHeaderRowAtTheTopOfEachPage = false` to
turn repetition off. Headerless object tables keep every row as body data; loading an
existing table does not add a repeating header. HTML conversion preserves source
body/header rows, and PDF import honours `RepeatHeaderRows`, including with Modern
tables.

`Bold = false` and `Italic = false` now explicitly disable inherited emphasis
instead of removing the direct setting. This lets regular text override a
bold table header or an italic paragraph style.

Native DOC borders and fills approximate RGB colours outside its 16-colour
palette. A native save rejects these changes with an `OfficeConversionException`
whose report carries `word-doc-color-approximated`; set `WordSaveOptions.AllowLoss`
to accept them. DOC conversion reports carry the same approximation while
keeping tables editable. DOCX retains the authored RGB colours.

A table of contents created with `AddTableOfContent` now stores its heading
entries when the document is saved, so viewers that do not update fields show
it; Word still refreshes the field on open. Paragraph counts after loading
include the `_Toc` bookmarks those entries add to each listed heading.

`AddEquation(string)` rejects OMML that contains elements outside Office Math,
such as `<m:int>`, with an `ArgumentException`. Write integrals and other n-ary
operators as `<m:nary>` with an `<m:chr>` character.

`WordPdfExportOptions.TrackedChanges` selects how tracked changes appear in PDF
output. The default, `WordPdfTrackedChangeView.Markup`, underlines insertions
and strikes through deletions in a revision colour. Set
`WordPdfExportOptions.TrackedChanges = WordPdfTrackedChangeView.Final` to show
insertions as current text and omit deletions. Only the Final view carries
`tracked-revisions-projected` when the source has tracked changes. Documents
without revisions render as before.

## PDF text replacement fonts

Replacement text that an embedded source-font subset cannot encode now uses
the detected standard substitute when its encoding covers the text. Inspect
`PdfTextEditResult.Warnings` for substitution and its possible effect on width
or letterforms. Set `PdfTextEditOptions.Font` to choose a standard face explicitly.
Unsupported shaping and text outside both encodings still fail before returning
an edited document; the source remains unchanged.

## PDF adapter package direction

`OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` now exports Word to PDF, and `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf`
exports PowerPoint to PDF. The package names stay the same while their direction
changes. For reconstruction, replace those references with
`OfficeIMO.Pdf.Word` or `OfficeIMO.Pdf.PowerPoint`. PDF-to-Excel reconstruction
moves from `OfficeIMO.Excel.Pdf` to `OfficeIMO.Pdf.Excel`; Excel PDF export stays
in `OfficeIMO.Excel.Pdf`.

Word page-image export also requires `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf`. Word and PowerPoint
format packages no longer bring the PDF engine. `OfficeIMO.Word.Markdown` no
longer brings the HTML engine. Install the `OfficeIMO` package for the common
formats, adapters, Reader handlers and file or batch conversions.

## Document search

Replace `Search-OfficeDocument -Query` with `-Pattern`. Patterns are regular
expressions by default; add `-SimpleMatch` to retain literal matching.
`-CaseSensitive` replaces `-MatchCase`. Use `-MaximumFiles`,
`-MaximumStoreItems`, `-MaximumResults` and `-ThrottleLimit` for the selection
and execution limits; zero removes each `Maximum*` ceiling. Search returns
individual `OfficeDocumentSearchMatch` objects for both paths and piped Reader
results, rather than an envelope with `Hits`. Use `-ErrorAction Stop` instead
of `-StopOnError`.

Recompile consumers of `OfficeIMO.Reader.Core`: `Search` now accepts an optional
`CancellationToken` after its options. Ordinary source calls keep working;
method-group bindings must include the token or use a lambda. C# search remains
literal unless `OfficeDocumentSearchOptions.UseRegularExpressions` is enabled.

## Unified C# lifecycle and conversions

Replace `MarkdownDoc` with `MarkdownDocument`, and `PdfReadDocument.Open(...)`
with `PdfDocument.Load(...)`. Load PDF bytes through a `MemoryStream`; reading
and inspection are available on the loaded document. Use `using` for documents,
including Markdown and PDF. PDF Markdown text extraction is `ExtractMarkdown()`;
`To{Target}` names return target models. Rename lifecycle settings to `{Format}CreateOptions`,
`{Format}LoadOptions` and `{Format}SaveOptions`; use the load options type's
`UntrustedDefaults` for external input. Inspection snapshots use `Info` names and
are reached through `Inspect()`. Shared `OfficeColor` and `OfficeColorRole` move
from `OfficeIMO.Drawing` to `OfficeIMO`.

Call conversions on their source. For example, replace
`WordDocument.FromMarkdown(text)` with
`MarkdownDocument.Parse(text).ToWord()`. Replace paired throwing and `...Result`
conversions with `To{Target}(options, out OfficeConversionReport report)` or
`SaveAs{Target}(pathOrStream, options)`. `ToHtml()` returns a string;
`To{Target}Async` returns `OfficeConversionResult<T>` with `Value` and `Report`.
`SaveAs{Target}` returns the shared report directly. Use `FailOnLoss` to reject
conversion loss before publication, or `report.ThrowIfLoss()` when reviewing an
in-memory result. Native saves reject loss unless their save options explicitly
set `AllowLoss`.

Handle conversion serialization or publication failures through
`OfficeConversionException.Report`; completed findings remain available and
`InnerException` identifies the underlying write failure. Invalid destination
arguments are checked before conversion and retain their argument exceptions.
Word-to-Markdown omission reports include skipped headers, footers, page breaks
and unsupported content even when warning text is suppressed. `FailOnLoss`
rejects these findings before publishing Markdown or its image/SVG sidecars;
analysis leaves sidecars unpublished.

Replace `OfficeWorkflow.Convert`, `OfficeDocumentPdfConverter` and the
`*ToPdfBytes` helpers with `OfficeConverter.Convert` or `ConvertAsync`. For bytes,
pass caller-owned input and output streams with their `OfficeDocumentFormat`
values. For batches, use `OfficeBatchOptions` and read the flattened
`OfficeBatchReport.Summary` and `Items`. `MaxParallelism` replaces
`MaximumConcurrency`; `ResumeFrom` names the checkpoint manifest file rather
than its directory. Tier 2 applications call `OfficeWorkflow.RegisterConversions()`;
iWork applications also call `IWorkWorkflow.RegisterConversions()`.

Saved jobs use `OfficeBatchOptions.Save` and `Load`; reports use
`OfficeBatchReport.Save` and `Load`. The saved-definition and report schemas are
version 2. Recreate version 1 job definitions from their reviewed input, output,
checkpoint and conversion settings; version 1 reports are not version 2 input.
Relative paths resolve against the saved job's directory. Password references
are properties on `OfficeBatchOptions`; literal passwords remain runtime-only.

Every existing library framework remains supported in 3.6. The front door and
both Workflows packages also support `netstandard2.0`, `net8.0`, `net10.0` and
`net472` on Windows. Modern-only optional engines retain their framework limits.

## Word field layout pagination

Select the native pagination engine through `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` when refreshing
page references or table-of-contents page numbers:

```csharp
using OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf;

document.UpdateFields(new WordFieldUpdateOptions {
    UpdateTablesOfContents = true
}.WithPdfLayoutPagination());
```

`WithPdfLayoutPagination()` copies the supplied options and selects the converter
explicitly. Calls that set `UseLayoutPagination = true` also need this selection.
The Word package keeps its PDF-independent field refresh based on explicit breaks.


## PDF AcroForm collision names

PDF merge with `Forms = Combine` and page import rename colliding field namespaces
with underscore suffixes: `Shared_source2`, then `Shared_source2_2`, instead of
`Shared.source2` and `Shared.source2.2`. Periods separate actual parent and child
field names. Hierarchical collisions rename the shared parent once, preserving
siblings such as `Parent_source2.First` and `Parent_source2.Second`.
Update field-name lookups or saved form-data mappings that depend on the old
suffixes; merge reports list the resulting names. To retain fields from documents
containing periods in a single partial field name, regenerate them from their
original sources before composing them again. `Forms = KeepPrimary` remains
the general merge default. Attachment and destination naming is unchanged.

## PowerShell Excel image URLs

`Add-OfficeExcelImage -Url` and `Add-OfficeExcelImageFromUrl -Url` now accept
HTTP and HTTPS URLs only. To add a local image, use `Add-OfficeExcelImage -Path`
with its file path instead of passing a `file:` URL. This keeps local file reads
behind the explicit path parameter.

## XML Spreadsheet defined-name limit

XML Spreadsheet import now admits at most 10,000 defined names by default. If
you import a trusted workbook with more names, set
`ExcelSpreadsheetXmlOptions.MaxNames` to the required positive limit. Imports
that exceed the configured limit fail before the names are materialized.

## Stroke geometry projection limits

Raster and gradient stroke projection limits cumulative copied and generated
points to two million per projection. Excessive expansion raises
`NotSupportedException`; simplify the geometry or dash pattern before
exporting it. PDF header/footer and link-bounds inspection uses a tighter
65,536-point budget. An exhausted inspection records unassessed clipping or
retains conservative clickable bounds while preserving native PDF paint.

## PDF content limits and redaction plans

`PdfReadLimits.MaxContentNestingDepth` also bounds nested marked-content scopes
(`BMC` and `BDC`). `MaxContentOperands` also bounds the cumulative dash-array
entries projected during one page operation, including nested forms. If you
set custom limits, account for these operations as well as lexical operands
and form nesting. Over-complex input raises `PdfReadLimitException`; simplify
the input or adjust the relevant limit for a trusted workload.

Rotation normalization rejects destination coordinates or zoom operands that
resolve to values other than numbers or `null`. Repair invalid destination
operands before calling `Pages.NormalizeRotation`.

SVG images normalized for PDF embedding have a cumulative raster-work limit:
paint bounding boxes may visit at most 256 times the output pixel count, and
contour crossings share a 512-million-work ceiling across nested renders.
`TryPrepareImageBytes` returns `false` with a reason when the limit is exceeded;
simplify excessive overdraw before embedding the image.

Matched-glyph redaction includes clipping-only text in its search and reports
unsupported clipping modes in the plan instead of silently omitting them.
Check `PdfRedactionPlan.IsReviewable` and inspect `Findings` before applying
the plan; a matching clipping-mode span requires a supported redaction strategy.
## Excel worksheet copies keep drawings, comments and links

`CopyWorksheet`, `CopyWorksheetFrom` with `ExcelWorksheetCopyMode.Package` and package-mode `MergeWorkbookFrom` now keep the copied sheet's images, charts, shapes, legacy and threaded comments, header/footer images, background picture and external hyperlinks. Earlier versions removed them. Copied threaded comments receive new ids, and the people they mention are added to the target workbook. Code that removed these features after copying, or that expected the copy to have none, should remove them explicitly with the sheet's comment, image and hyperlink APIs. See the [worksheet copy contract](OfficeIMO.Excel/COMPATIBILITY.md#workbook-capabilities).

## Word document append

`WordDocument.AppendDocument` now keeps the page setup of each document: the destination's final section properties become a section break before the appended content, which starts in its own section (a new page unless the source section says otherwise). To continue the appended content in the destination's section, as a workaround that moved the destination's closing `w:sectPr` did before, pass `new WordDocumentMergeOptions { SectionMode = WordMergeSectionMode.UseDestinationSections }`.

Source styles now match destination styles by name before id, so a source style with a different id but the same name (for example a localized `Heading 1`) uses the destination style instead of being copied alongside it. Appended footnotes, endnotes and comments are copied with renumbered ids, and source bookmarks whose names already exist in the destination are renamed with a numeric suffix (`Intro` becomes `Intro_1`); hyperlinks and fields in the appended content follow the new name.

`WordTableOfContent.RefreshEntries()` also includes paragraphs whose style, or a style it is based on, sets an outline level 1-9 when the TOC uses `\u` (as Word's default TOC does), and heading styles copied by a merge such as `heading 1_0`.

## JavaScript CanopyX pivot captures

Pass explicit frozen `request.pivot` captures through the optional CanopyX export entry point. They retain their own precomputed numeric values, formats and row/column outlines. Do not supply ordinary grouping metadata, replacement outline callbacks, an Excel table or a recalculating footer for the same pivot. PDF/CSV preserve the complete static projection and report `PIVOT_OUTLINES_XLSX_ONLY`; XLSX retains the interactive outlines with summaries above and left of details. Ordinary record/grouped exports keep their existing behavior.

## Reading running text from RTF-generated PDFs

RTF PDF headers and footers use rich running content and are marked as PDF
pagination artifacts. To inspect their text with the logical reader, enable
`PdfLoadOptions.IncludeArtifactText`:

```csharp
using var input = new MemoryStream(bytes);
using var document = PdfDocument.Load(input,
    new PdfLoadOptions { IncludeArtifactText = true });
var read = document.Read();
```

The default reader continues to exclude artifact text. Explicit header/footer
presentation overrides retain the plain-text projection. Ordinary uncropped
running pictures written through the RTF-to-Word bridge use VML; callers that
inspect raw Word XML should handle `w:pict` as well as DrawingML `w:drawing`.

## Conversion batch outcomes and saved jobs

CLI `workflow batch` now fails when no conversions are selected, including an
all-skipped folder. Add `--allow-empty` only when an empty run is intentional.
The default aggregate JSON remains unchanged; choose `--format json` for a
versioned per-file report or `--format ndjson` for streamed item outcomes.
Terminal discovery failures now return retained counts and `FailureSummary`
(`failureSummary` in versioned JSON); check this alongside per-file failures.

PSWriteOffice's `ConvertTo-OfficeDocument` and `Export-OfficeDocumentPdf` batches
now emit an error for failed items or an empty selection. `-ErrorAction Stop`
therefore stops a script after the batch summary is assigned. Completed outputs
remain available. Inspect the summary or streamed item results when continuing
after errors, and use `-AllowEmpty` only for intentional empty selections.

Saved conversion jobs resolve relative paths against the job file, independently
of the working directory. Keep job files outside their source, output and
checkpoint trees. Use environment-variable references for source passwords;
literal password values and unsupported native renderer settings cannot be
captured in the portable job format.

Newly captured relative paths use `/` on every operating system. Re-save older
Windows definitions before moving them to another operating system if their
relative paths contain `\`; Unix treats that character as part of a filename.
Run reports are optional evidence and do not change checkpoint compatibility.

## Removed obsolete image and HTML capability aliases

Replace `WordImage.BlackWiteMode` with `WordImage.BlackWhiteMode`. The enum and
image black-and-white behavior are unchanged.

`HtmlTargetCapabilityContract` accepts `HtmlToTargetCapabilityContract` and an
optional `TargetToHtmlCapabilityContract`. Replace the constructor that took a
single shared set of profiles and feature classifications with these directional
contracts. Classify each direction independently and provide its diagnostics
contract; pass `null` for `targetToHtml` when no reverse conversion exists.

Read the following members from `contract.HtmlToTarget` for import, or from
`contract.TargetToHtml` for reverse export:

- `IoAndAsyncBoundary`
- `Profiles`
- `SupportedFeatures`, `ApproximatedFeatures`, and `UnsupportedFeatures`
- `GetSupport(feature)`

The former target-level aliases have been removed. Check `TargetToHtml` for
`null` before reading a reverse contract. There is no combined profile list:
select the direction that the application actually uses.

## PSWriteOffice file and workflow APIs

Build and publish PSWriteOffice through `Build/Build-Release.ps1` so its version
and engine payloads follow the coordinated NuGet, PowerShell Gallery and GitHub
release. Source, examples and tests live under `PowerShell/PSWriteOffice`.

`New-OfficeWord -TemplatePath ... -NoSave` and its Excel equivalent leave the
template and destination untouched until an explicit save. Scripts that depended
on the earlier implicit template copy must call the corresponding `Save` command.

`Set-OfficePdfCompliance` and `Set-OfficePdfElectronicInvoice` configure new PDF
documents inside the PDF DSL. Their unsupported `-Document` parameter sets and
ineffective `-PassThru` parameters have been removed. Use the supported PDF
inspection and conversion commands for existing files.

Scalar file readers accept `FullName`/`LiteralPath` aliases and `FileInfo`
pipelines, resolve FileSystem PSDrives, and reject other providers. Input is
literal; expand wildcards with `Get-ChildItem` first.

`Export-OfficeExcel -InputObject <DataSet> -Append` and `-ClearSheet` no longer
guess that a lone table named `Budget` owns an existing `Budget (2)` worksheet.
They use or create `Budget` instead. Name the source table `Budget (2)` when
that suffixed worksheet is the intended target. Multiple tables in the same
DataSet that normalize to the same worksheet name still receive successive
suffixes.

`ConvertTo-OfficeDocument` provides catalog-driven single and batch conversion
with destination protection, bounds and structured evidence. It requires
PowerShell 7.4. Existing format-specific commands retain their documented host
support. Model invoice validation works on Windows PowerShell 5.1;
authority-rule validation requires PowerShell 7.4.

Release credentials use `NUGET_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `PSGALLERY_API_KEY_FILE`
and `GITHUB_TOKEN_FILE`; workstation-specific secret paths are no longer used.
See [building and releasing](Docs/building-and-releasing.md) for file overrides
and portable default locations.

## ChartForgeX 3 and CodeGlyphX 3

`OfficeIMO.ChartForgeX` and `OfficeIMO.ChartForgeX.Markdown` use ChartForgeX 3.0.0. Prepare visuals with the shared `VisualTheme` and `VisualThemeMode` API. Replace legacy theme factories such as `TopologyTheme.Light()` with `WithThemeMode(VisualThemeMode.Light)`, or pass a paired theme to `WithTheme(...)`. Customize theme colors through `ConfigureTheme(...)`; for example, `theme.Light.Surface` supplies the topology card fill. The OfficeIMO conversion and document-placement APIs are unchanged.

`OfficeIMO.Drawing.CodeGlyphX` requires CodeGlyphX 3.x (`[3.0.0, 4.0.0)`). Update an application's direct CodeGlyphX reference to the same major version when using this bridge. Create QR codes with `QR.Encode(...)` and `QrEncodingOptions`, and use the shared `CodeGlyphX.Rendering.QrModuleShape` enum for styled modules.

## Strict PDF standards helpers

`PdfCreateOptions.UsePdfA(...)` and `UsePdfUa(...)` enable the strict compliance gate. Saving rejects missing font embedding, accessibility prerequisites and incompatible combined profile declarations; every declared A/UA profile is checked against the saved bytes. Applications that only prepare metadata can use `ConfigurePdfAGroundwork(...)` and `ConfigurePdfUaGroundwork(...)` instead. External validation remains necessary for a conformance claim on an exact artifact.

PDF/A-4, PDF/A-4e, PDF/A-4f and PDF/UA-2 use PDF 2.0. PDF/A-4 metadata lives in XMP; callers reading only trailer Info fields should read `PdfDocument.Load(bytes).Inspect().XmpMetadata`.

Hybrid invoice generation supports only PDF/A-3a, PDF/A-3b and PDF/A-3u, optionally combined with PDF/UA-1, and preserves those configured profiles. Replace PDF/A-4, PDF/A-4e or PDF/A-4f hybrid options with a supported PDF/A-3 profile, and replace PDF/UA-2 with PDF/UA-1 for hybrids. Use presentation-only output when invoice XML is not required; general PDF/A-4, PDF/A-4e and PDF/A-4f output remains available. Saved PDF/A-4f attachments cannot satisfy Factur-X/ZUGFeRD compliance proof.

## Lossless PDF optimization

The optimizer preserves XMP packets, embedded-file streams and output-intent ICC streams without changing their encoding or contents, and retains the source Info dictionary only when it exists. PDF/A-1 inputs reject object-stream or xref-stream settings; use `Balanced`, `Archival` or `Web`, or set `UseObjectStreams = false` and `XrefFormat = ClassicTable`. Inputs with filtered XMP metadata are rejected before output is written because the optimizer cannot both remove its filter and preserve the packet encoding. Object/xref-stream settings also reject unreadable XMP because its declared profile cannot be established safely; use classic cross references or supply metadata within the supported XML read limits. Signed files remain blocked: optimize before signing.

## PAdES signatures and visible text

`PdfCmsExternalSigner` honors the prepared subfilter. `CadesDetached` creates PAdES baseline CMS with a signing-certificate-v2 attribute and without CMS signing-time; SHA-1 and encapsulated content are rejected for this profile. RSA and ECDSA signing use platform key handles. `DetachedCms` retains its CMS signing-time behavior. Document timestamps require an RFC 3161 signer rather than the detached CMS adapter.

Visible text appearances require `PdfVisibleSignatureAppearanceOptions.Font` with an embedded TrueType font. Supply the font explicitly; the writer rejects missing fonts instead of emitting unembedded Helvetica. Image-only appearances with `ShowText = false` do not need a text font.

For B-T, provide `CmsSigningOptions.SignatureTimestampProvider`, for example `Rfc3161TimestampClient.GetTimestamp`. The client accepts caller-owned HTTP transport and trust policy, checks nonce, imprint and TSA signature, and returns the token for the CMS unsigned attribute. Optional evidence fetching uses `PdfLongTermValidationEnricher.EnrichAsync`; existing caller-supplied DSS/VRI enrichment remains available. Embedded certificates and revocation data alone do not establish a complete trusted B-LT validation path.

## PDF graphics, images and stream compression

Direct PDF authoring compresses page content with Flate by default. Set `PdfCreateOptions.CompressContentStreams = false` when a tool needs plain page operators. ICC profiles, embedded files and widget appearances are compressed independently; XMP packets remain uncompressed. Tools inspecting PDF streams must decode their declared filters before reading their content. `PdfAttachmentInfo.SizeBytes` remains the encoded stream size; use `DeclaredSizeBytes` for the original size declared in attachment parameters, or extract the payload when its actual decoded size is required.

`OfficeIMO.Reader.Pdf` attachment `sizeBytes` and total-size metadata also describe encoded streams. `encodedSizeBytes` names that value explicitly; `declaredSizeBytes` carries the untrusted payload-size claim when present. Metadata inspection does not decode attachments.

Image authoring applies EXIF rotation and mirroring through placement matrices. Previously unoriented images can rotate or mirror, and their intrinsic dimensions and resolution axes can swap. JPEG DCT payloads, PNG sample depth, ICC profiles, transparency masks and image sharing are retained through orientation changes. Supported PNG and JPEG ICC profiles use ICCBased colour spaces; indexed PNGs keep their palettes. Sixteen-bit PNG samples are retained in PDF 1.5 and newer. PDF 1.4 output rounds them to eight bits. Crops and authored mirrors or rotations compose around the target frame. Visible signature images now follow the same resource-allocation and target-version rules.

Authored-layout reports now include glyph and inline paint overhang, rotated and viewport cells, paragraph frames and free-text boxes. Existing report consumers can receive warnings for previously silent clipping. Enlarge the affected frame or adjust its content; geometry that cannot be inspected within the bounded contract is reported as unassessed. Enabling these diagnostics does not change PDF text emission.

Supported SVG images embedded in drawings retain vector paths, gradients, clipping and text. Tiling patterns use reusable PDF pattern cells. Expanded link annotations count against a shared generation budget derived from the existing pattern `maximumTileCount` limits, including nested and running content. Canvas gradients interpolate premultiplied colour channels, avoiding dark fringes beside transparent stops; imported SVG/XPS gradients retain their producer's separate colour/alpha interpolation. Regenerate image baselines that relied on the earlier rasterized SVG or canvas-gradient appearance.

PDF page images and SVG exports retain horizontal and vertical text reflection, including inside clips. Regenerate previews of mirrored text that previously disappeared or used only its baseline rotation.

## Image encoding defaults

PNG and lossless WebP now default to `OfficeImageEncodingEffort.Balanced`. This replaces exhaustive candidate searches with bounded heuristics and one main compression plan. Set `RasterEncoding.Png.Effort` or `RasterEncoding.Webp.Effort` to `Smallest` to select the exhaustive compressor, or to `Fast` for lower encode cost. Direct codec option objects expose the same `Effort` property. Pixels remain lossless at every level; compressed bytes and sizes can change. PNG effort applies to `Compression = Optimal`; explicit `Fastest` and `Stored` compression retain their existing contracts. Lossy WebP quality remains separate.

PNG optimal output chooses exact grayscale, grayscale-alpha, RGB, RGBA, or indexed samples instead of requiring a fixed channel layout. Palette transparency retains every original RGBA value. Generated PNGs also declare sRGB with matching gamma and chromaticities; a supplied ICC profile replaces those declarations through `EncodeWithMetadata`. Consumers must read IHDR rather than assume RGBA. Encoded bytes and image baselines can change while decoded pixels remain identical. `EncodeScanlines` and `CreateFromCompressedScanlines` retain the caller-selected layout and do not add automatic color declarations. The public raster model remains eight-bit; use `OfficePngWriter.EncodeRgba64` to encode sixteen-bit source samples directly.

JPEG enables optimized Huffman tables by default. Quality 85, 4:4:4 sampling, and sequential scans remain the defaults, and decoded pixels are unchanged by Huffman optimization. Set `OfficeJpegEncodeOptions.OptimizeHuffman = false` to retain standard tables and the lower-memory MCU-at-a-time path.

SVG non-interpolated images are embedded rasters with sampling hints instead of pixel rectangles. Consumers that inspect SVG structure must accept `<image>` and data URIs. Supported already-painted text can become paths; opt into eligible ordinary text paths with `SvgTextAsPaths`. Paths preserve appearance and logical accessibility labels but are not selectable SVG text.

## PowerPoint PDF and slide images

PowerPoint image export stays in `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint`; forward PDF conversion lives in `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf`. Replace `ToPng`, `ToJpeg`, `ToSvg` and the image builders with `slide.ToImage(options)`, setting `options.Format`. `SaveAsImage(pathOrStream, options)` and `SaveAsImages(folder, options)` return `OfficeConversionReport`; async in-memory rendering returns `OfficeConversionResult<byte[]>`. Batch slide numbers and hidden-slide selection belong in `PowerPointImageExportOptions`.

`AddTextBox` creates an ordinary text shape. Set `PlaceholderType` and `PlaceholderIndex` explicitly when creating a template placeholder. Ordinary text shapes on slide layouts remain visible inherited content; structural placeholder prompts supply styles and geometry.

Image options carry font settings and fidelity diagnostics use the shared catalog. `CreateVisualSnapshot().TextSpans` exposes text and geometry. PDF options remain on the PDF adapter.

PowerPoint page-image batches retain zero-based `SequenceIndex` and the selected batch's `SequenceCount`, alongside the original slide identity. Snapshot creation enforces `RenderTimeout` through the shared image-export deadline and reports `OfficeImageExportTimeoutException`.

DrawingML normal autofit applies stored font scaling and line-spacing reduction, or computes shrinking when the scale is absent. Shape autofit grows the exported frame. Fixed frames retain overflowing text without ellipses and report overflow; the slide edge clips visible painting. Tables use PowerPoint cell insets and grow rows for content. Image output therefore changes from the former preview renderer. Embedded-image byte limits also apply to the PDF layout; the aggregate limit covers the selected conversion, rather than resetting for each rendered image.

PDF-to-PowerPoint extension-call syntax is unchanged. Static calls move from `PowerPointPdfConverterExtensions.ToPowerPointPresentation*` and `.SaveAsPowerPoint*` to `PdfPowerPointConverterExtensions`, which remains in `OfficeIMO.PowerPoint.Pdf`.

Layout and master placeholder prompts are not slide content. Create a concrete slide placeholder to display its text or field; it inherits the template's geometry and style. Ordinary layout and master artwork remains visible.

## Markdown, Word and HTML conversion output

Regenerate visual baselines for Markdown to HTML, Markdown to Word, Word to HTML and HTML rendering; the defaults below change layout and markup.

- `MarkdownDocument.SaveAsHtml(path)` and `SaveAsHtmlAsync(path)` without options write a complete HTML document with a stylesheet. Pass `new MarkdownHtmlExportOptions()` to keep writing a fragment.
- `MarkdownHtmlStyle.Clean`, the default style, no longer switches to the Word stylesheet when no `Theme` is set. It declares the `--office-*` theme tokens and uses them. Set `Style = MarkdownHtmlStyle.Word` for the previous look. Styled output right-aligns table columns of numbers that have no authored alignment; `Plain` keeps the source alignment.
- Markdown to Word writes code blocks with a `CodeLang_<language>` paragraph style, wraps headings in bookmarks and turns `#fragment` links into in-document links. Relative image paths resolve against `BaseUri` or the Markdown file's folder. Images that cannot be embedded are reported as `image-skipped-by-policy` or `image-load-failed` omissions, so `HasLoss` and `FailOnLoss` see them; set `AllowLocalImages = true` to embed local files. `WordMarkdownImageLayoutOptions.FitMode` defaults to `ContextContentWidth`; set `None` for natural image size. New documents get theme heading and Normal styles, quotes get a left rule and table columns are sized from their content.
- Word to HTML rebuilds a table of contents from the headings and reports `toc-regenerated-from-headings`. Monospace runs become `<code>`, and the default stylesheet uses the theme tokens.
- HTML rendering keeps the monospace default for `code`, `pre`, `kbd` and `samp` when an ancestor sets a font family, in Document mode as well; set `font-family: inherit` on them for the previous result. `font-variant: small-caps` is synthesized from smaller capitals. An image that does not load and has no size takes the space of its alternative text. HTML to PDF loads `file:` resources when `PdfResourcePolicy.AllowLocalFileAccess` is true. `HtmlRenderMathMlSourceNormalized` is now an `Info` diagnostic.

## HTML default-font metrics

Raw HTML rendering retains the configured default font when installed-font fallback is permitted. Its selected face can change advances, baselines, wrapping and page counts compared with the earlier estimated layout. Register complete font bytes and set `AllowSystemFontFallback = false` for a fixed font selection across hosts.

Visible raw text measured without a selected program reports `HtmlRenderFontMetricsEstimated`. `RequireNoLoss` rejects that approximation. Supply a covering face through `Fonts` or a policy-approved `@font-face`, or use `AllowDiagnosedLoss` and inspect the diagnostic. Explicit PDF default-font registrations retain their bytes for shared layout and painting; caller-supplied CSS faces keep ownership.

## Office conversion fonts and Word page images

`WordParagraph.AddFootNote` rejects header and footer paragraphs, including their table cells, with `InvalidOperationException` before changing the document. Place footnote references in body paragraphs or body table cells. Earlier calls in running stories could produce invalid DOCX; existing malformed inputs remain subject to conversion loss reporting.

The balanced PDF resource policy embeds installed document fonts by default for Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Markdown. HTML-to-PDF uses `PdfResourcePolicy.CreateLibraryFontDefault()`: library-selected installed fonts are embedded, while CSS-selected host fonts require an explicit `AllowDocumentFontEmbedding` permission. Fonts supplied by installed Office applications on macOS are discoverable. Output sizes, line breaks and pagination can change as embedded faces replace standard Helvetica fallbacks. Review substitution diagnostics and the `font-embedding-cost` entries for the actual font payload cost. Set `ResourcePolicy = PdfResourcePolicy.CreatePortableDeterministic()` or supply a fixed rendering profile when output must not depend on host fonts.

`PdfOptions.EmbedDefaultFonts = false` disables automatic embedding for standard PDF font slots. HTML fonts retained by the render engine and explicitly supplied fonts keep their separate resource policy.

HTML page images backed by embedded PDF fonts retain their exact glyph contours
in SVG, with source text in accessible labels. Code that inspects these images
must handle paths rather than assuming every word is an SVG `<text>` element or
an `OfficeDrawingText`. Use the retained HTML scene for text and style inspection;
outlined SVG glyphs are not selectable text.

Word image export (`ToPng`, `ToJpeg`, `ToSvg`, `ExportImages`, and their fluent builders) now uses the same page layout and font policy as Word-to-PDF. Regenerate preview baselines: page counts, line breaks, styles and borders can change, and the preview renderer no longer shortens text with an ellipsis. Set `WordImageExportOptions.LayoutOptions` to the same `WordPdfExportOptions` used for PDF export when customizing layout.

`OfficeIMO.Word` now references `OfficeIMO.Pdf`, which depends only on `OfficeIMO.Core`; no external runtime dependency is added. Forward conversion APIs and `WordPdfExportOptions` move from the `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf` assembly to `OfficeIMO.Word`, retaining their namespace. Recompile consumers; PDF-to-Word import still requires `OfficeIMO.Word.Pdf`.

`WordDocumentVisualInfo.Fragments` and the guessed source-block fragment/region types are removed. Use `TextSpans` for text and geometry from the actual laid-out page, in PDF user-space coordinates. `IncludeDocumentContent`, builder `IncludeContent`/`WithoutContent`, and preview-specific `WordImageExportDiagnosticCodes` are removed. PowerShell callers should remove `-IncludeDocumentContent` from `New-OfficeWordImageOptions`; Word page images always render document content. Export diagnostics now carry the same conversion and rendering codes as the PDF-backed route. Skipped unsupported objects are classified as omissions, so `RequireNoOmissions` rejects them on both routes; font, wrapping and appearance fallbacks remain approximations. An out-of-range page index throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` instead of producing an empty preview.

With Reader Word `IncludePageLocations`, `Pages` and normalized `Blocks` now contain visible page text lines with PDF user-space baseline extents, rather than source paragraph/table fragments. Their IDs are page/line-specific; logical text remains in `Chunks` and authored tables/links remain at document scope. Page search and Markdown follow the rendered lines. This projection reports `officeimo.reader.word.rich-v5` and remains opt-in.

Inline header and footer pictures retain their height and reserve body space. Empty table paragraphs retain their mark's minimum line height, including explicit cell margins. Supported non-wrapping floating pictures retain paragraph/margin anchors and signed offsets. Pictures extending beyond a page retain their placement and report clipping instead of entering document flow.

Header/footer SmartArt authoring and reading now use relationships on the containing story for diagram data, layout, colours, quick style and cached drawing. Regenerate DOCX files whose header/footer diagrams were authored with relationships only on the main document part; saving an existing malformed file does not relocate those parts automatically. Body diagrams retain their existing relationship ownership.

## Markdown PDF and page images

Markdown PDF export preserves code-block indentation, including consecutive tabs, and uses the same monospace font selection for inline code and fenced code. Footnote references are superscript internal links; definitions follow the document body. Parent ordered items following nested lists remain separate items in both HTML and PDF output.

`PdfTextFallbackFeatures.Default` includes `MultilingualFonts`. Converters using this shared default can embed installed fallback fonts for Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, and Hebrew under their resource policy. Rebuild consumers that compiled the enum constant into their own options. Select `None`, or individual flags without `MultilingualFonts`, when exact font selection is required. Font coverage still depends on the permitted fonts available to the host.

RTF PDF export exposes `RtfToPdfOptions.TextFallbacks` with the same default. Installed fallback faces cover characters missing from the authored font; system-font access remains controlled by `ResourcePolicy.AllowSystemFontEmbedding`.

`PdfParagraphStyle.TextWhitespaceMode` overrides whitespace handling for one paragraph without changing the document's prose. A null value inherits `PdfCreateOptions.TextWhitespaceMode`.

## PDF text output and embedded fonts

Generated PDF text applies pair kerning by default for standard and embedded fonts, so line widths, wrapping and page breaks can change. Set `PdfCreateOptions.TextKerning = false` to keep the previous unkerned advances. Regenerate visual baselines that pinned earlier line breaks.

Line wrapping follows Unicode line breaking (UAX #14). Words can now break after hyphens and slashes, at zero-width spaces and between CJK characters, so a token such as `buyer-service-1` can wrap as `buyer-` / `service-1`. `PdfCreateOptions.UseAutomaticHyphenation(language)` adds opt-in US English and German pattern hyphenation; it replaces any `UseTextHyphenationDictionary` configuration, and the last one configured applies.

Right-to-left and Arabic text is shaped and ordered automatically, without configuring a shaping provider. Glyphs are written in visual order, and pure right-to-left runs no longer carry a run-wide `ActualText`; their Unicode text comes from the font's `ToUnicode` map. Logical text extraction is unchanged.

Text is written as one `TJ` array per run, with numeric kerning and justification adjustments, instead of per-glyph `Tj` operators with individual text matrices. `ActualText` is written only for clusters that `ToUnicode` cannot express. Tools that parse OfficeIMO content streams should accept `TJ` arrays.

Embedded font names carry the standard six-letter subset tag, for example `ABCDEF+Arial`. TrueType subsets are renumbered compactly and mapped through `/CIDToGIDMap`.
